Riverwalk Augusta GA Guide: Your Complete Local's Handbook

Welcome to Augusta, Georgia—a city where Southern charm meets riverfront beauty. If you're planning a trip, the Riverwalk Augusta GA guide is your essential resource for exploring one of the city's most beloved attractions. Stretching along the Savannah River, the Augusta Riverwalk offers a picturesque blend of history, nature, and entertainment. Whether you're a first-time visitor or a local looking to rediscover your city, this guide will walk you through everything you need to know.

What is the Riverwalk Augusta GA?

The Augusta Riverwalk is a scenic promenade that runs along the banks of the Savannah River in downtown Augusta. It's a vibrant area featuring beautifully landscaped gardens, historic sites, and plenty of spots to relax and take in the view. The Riverwalk is part of the larger Augusta Canal National Heritage Area, which tells the story of the city's industrial past and its role in the Civil War.

One of the best things about the Riverwalk is that it's free and open to the public year-round. It's a favorite spot for walkers, joggers, and cyclists, and it hosts numerous events and festivals throughout the year.

Top Attractions Along the Riverwalk

1. Augusta Canal Discovery Center

Start your journey at the Augusta Canal Discovery Center, located at 1450 Greene Street. This interactive museum offers exhibits on the canal's history and its impact on Augusta. You can also take a guided boat tour along the canal to learn more about the area's heritage.

2. The Augusta Museum of History

Just a short walk from the Riverwalk, the Augusta Museum of History at 560 Reynolds Street is a must-visit. It houses exhibits on local history, including the story of Augusta native James Brown. The museum provides context for the region's development and its cultural significance.

3. Riverwalk Amphitheater

This outdoor venue hosts concerts, festivals, and community events. Check the schedule during your visit—you might catch a live performance with the river as your backdrop.

4. The Boyhood Home of President Woodrow Wilson

History buffs will appreciate the Woodrow Wilson Boyhood Home at 419 7th Street. The 28th President spent his formative years here, and guided tours offer a glimpse into his early life.

5. Augusta Common

This central green space connects the Riverwalk to downtown Augusta. It's a great place to relax, have a picnic, or let the kids run around. The Common also hosts events like the Augusta Market, a weekly farmers market.

Dining and Nightlife Near the Riverwalk

After a day of exploring, you'll want to refuel. The Riverwalk area boasts a variety of dining options, from casual cafes to upscale restaurants.

  • The Boll Weevil Cafe and Sweetery: A local favorite for Southern comfort food and decadent desserts. Located at 10 James Brown Boulevard, it's a short walk from the Riverwalk.
  • Manuel's Bread Cafe: Situated in the Riverwood Mansion at 5050 Riverwood Drive, this cafe offers fresh baked goods and light lunches in a historic setting.
  • Nacho Mama's: For a fun, casual meal, head to this Tex-Mex spot at 976 Broad Street. Their margaritas are legendary.
  • Frog Hollow Tavern: A farm-to-table restaurant at 1282 Broad Street, perfect for a special dinner. Their menu changes seasonally.

For nightlife, check out the bars and music venues along Broad Street, many of which feature live music on weekends.

Events and Festivals on the Riverwalk

The Riverwalk is the heart of many of Augusta's biggest events. Here are a few you shouldn't miss:

  • Augusta Pride Festival: Held in October, this event celebrates diversity with music, food, and vendors.
  • Arts in the Heart of Augusta: A September festival featuring art, food, and performances from around the world.
  • Fourth of July Celebration: Enjoy fireworks over the Savannah River—a spectacular sight.
  • Ironman 70.3 Augusta: Watch athletes swim, bike, and run through the city, with portions of the race along the river.

Check the Augusta Convention & Visitors Bureau website for a full calendar of events.

Outdoor Activities Along the Riverwalk

If you're an outdoor enthusiast, the Riverwalk offers plenty of opportunities to get active.

Walking and Jogging

The paved path is perfect for a morning jog or an evening stroll. The route is well-lit and safe, making it accessible for all ages.

Cycling

Bring your bike or rent one from a local shop like Chain Reaction Bicycles at 3116 Washington Road. The Riverwalk connects to other trails, including the Augusta Canal Towpath, which offers miles of scenic riding.

Kayaking and Paddling

For a different perspective, get out on the water. Several outfitters offer kayak rentals and guided tours. If you're staying with us at KJ Augusta Rentals' Entire River House, you'll have kayaks available right on the property—a perfect way to explore the river at your own pace.

Where to Stay Near the Riverwalk

To make the most of your Riverwalk visit, stay close by. KJ Augusta Rentals offers premium waterfront accommodations on the Savannah River, just a short drive from downtown.

  • Entire River House: Sleeps up to 16, with a saltwater pool, kayaks, and a fire pit on 3 acres.
  • Upstairs River House: A cozy option for smaller groups, with stunning river views.
  • River Suite: Perfect for couples, featuring modern amenities and direct river access.

Each property provides a peaceful retreat after a day of exploring, with easy access to all that Augusta has to offer.

Practical Tips for Visiting the Riverwalk

  • Parking: There are several public parking decks near the Riverwalk, including the Reynolds Street Parking Deck at 900 Reynolds Street. Parking is free on weekends and after 5 PM on weekdays.
  • Best Time to Visit: Spring and fall offer mild temperatures and beautiful scenery. Summers can be hot and humid, so plan outdoor activities for early morning or late evening.
  • Accessibility: The Riverwalk is wheelchair-accessible, with paved paths and ramps.
  • Safety: The area is well-patrolled, but as with any public space, stay aware of your surroundings, especially at night.
  • What to Bring: Comfortable shoes, sunscreen, water, and a camera—the views are worth capturing.

Nearby Attractions Worth a Visit

Beyond the Riverwalk, Augusta has plenty more to offer. Here are a few nearby attractions:

  • Augusta National Golf Club: Home of the Masters Tournament, a must-see for golf fans (though public access is limited).
  • Phinizy Swamp Nature Park: A beautiful wetland area with trails and wildlife viewing, located at 1858 Lock and Dam Road.
  • Augusta Downtown Historic District: Stroll through historic streets lined with antebellum architecture and charming shops.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the Riverwalk Augusta GA free to visit?

Yes, the Riverwalk is free and open to the public daily from dawn to dusk.

Are dogs allowed on the Riverwalk?

Yes, leashed dogs are welcome. Please clean up after your pet.

What is the best time of year to visit the Riverwalk?

Spring (March–May) and fall (September–November) offer the most comfortable weather for walking and outdoor activities.

Are there restaurants on the Riverwalk?

While there are no restaurants directly on the Riverwalk, several dining options are just a short walk away in downtown Augusta.

Can you fish from the Riverwalk?

Fishing is allowed in certain areas along the Savannah River, but a Georgia fishing license is required. Check local regulations for specifics.

With this Riverwalk Augusta GA guide, you're ready to explore one of the South's most charming riverfronts. Whether you're here for a weekend or an extended stay, the Riverwalk offers a perfect blend of relaxation and adventure. And when you're ready to unwind, KJ Augusta Rentals provides the ideal home base for your Augusta getaway.
